slice: Remove redundant floating normalization through the existing UDF simplify hook
scope: Reuse ScalarUDFImpl::simplify to remove normalization around integer-to-floating casts, Decimal-to-DOUBLE casts and an existing SparkComparisonFloat call. Retain any FLOAT-to-DOUBLE widening. Add one parameterized Rust test; no new optimizer pass, execution node, dependency or benchmark harness.

provenance.source_note: Local Rust implementation in the existing helper. It uses the installed DataFusion 54.1.0 simplification interface and existing native casts; no new Sail code is imported.
provenance.before_build_dependencies: Identical to candidate_build.dependencies for every package ID, feature set and profile.
provenance.reference_note: The reference is the frozen 112-query baseline before the pure FLOAT/DOUBLE normalization extension, recorded by float-zero-comparisons-results.json. It already includes the older mixed Decimal/floating normalization helper. Only the three affected ANSI-true benchmark queries are timed with this reference.

correctness_argument.integer_casts: Signed and unsigned integer casts to FLOAT/DOUBLE cannot generate a negative zero or NaN. Keep the original cast, including any integer-to-FLOAT rounding.
correctness_argument.decimal_casts: Decimal coefficients and supported scales fit the nonzero DOUBLE range. The existing conversion cannot underflow a nonzero coefficient to negative zero, or create NaN. Decimal-to-FLOAT normalization remains because wide Decimal values can underflow.
correctness_argument.nested_calls: Normalization is idempotent. If an outer call also widens FLOAT to DOUBLE, replace only its normalization and preserve the widening cast.
correctness_argument.evaluation: Retain the original argument once; do not duplicate, eagerly evaluate or replace its cast/error/null handling.

performance_findings.execution: Explicit DOUBLE/Decimal short IN improves 5.806 to 4.234 ms (-27.08%); the pre-extension reference is 4.237 ms. FLOAT/DOUBLE projected IN improves 10.769 to 9.262 ms (-13.99%), versus a 9.144 ms reference. These two plans match the reference and execute within 0.01% of its instruction counts. The older mixed projected-IN case improves 9.353 to 9.120 ms (-2.49%), with 3.24% fewer instructions.
performance_findings.planning: FLOAT/DOUBLE projected-IN planning falls 1.480 to 1.423 ms, but remains 6.03% above the pre-extension reference. Decimal short-IN planning rises 0.711 to 0.754 ms (+0.044 ms, +6.12%), or +12.91% versus the pre-extension reference. The execution regression is removed there; planning overhead remains.

controls.note: All twelve control plans are unchanged. Their instruction changes stay below 0.12% in planning and 0.06% in execution. The unchanged projected-IN control has a large apparent elapsed-time improvement (-33.91%) with nearly identical instructions. As in previous runs, this timing variability is not counted as a patch benefit.

performance_findings.remaining: Pure floating comparisons and short IN lists over raw FLOAT/DOUBLE columns keep their normalizer, native set-lookup plan and measured prior overhead. This slice does not remove it or claim universal absence of regression.

performance_method: Identical 112-query Rust harness, dependency features/profiles and Arrow libraries. 1,048,576 outer rows, 511 inner rows, 8192-row batches, one partition. Four fresh processes per measured query/variant/phase, balanced before/after/reference/reference/after/before order repeated twice, rotated query order, CPU 2, two warmups, nine samples, retained results disabled. The reference runs only the three affected queries. Separate perf FIFO planning/execution intervals; instructions/cycles grouped at 100% running. Every timed result and plan equals its canonical correctness capture. All compilation and correctness runs finish, and all shared sources/executables are restored, before timing. Summaries are medians of four process medians.

import hashlib, json, os, shutil, subprocess
from pathlib import Path

p = Path(__file__).parent
h = Path('/tmp/delta-reader-spark-planning/round-constant/checkout/experiments/spark-sql')
sha = lambda file: hashlib.sha256(Path(file).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
cmd = ['cargo', 'build', '--release', '--offline', '--locked', '--config', str(p / 'override.toml'), '--example', 'decimal_bench', '--example', 'decimal_probe', '--bin', 'delta-reader-sail-extraction-probe', '--message-format=json', '-j', '3']
with (p / 'cargo.jsonl').open('w') as out, (p / 'build.log').open('w') as err:
    subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=h, env=os.environ | {'CARGO_TARGET_DIR': str(p.parent / 'integer-widening-sparse-owned-542a847/target')}, stdout=out, stderr=err, check=True)
artifacts = [json.loads(line) for line in (p / 'cargo.jsonl').read_text().splitlines()]
artifacts = [r for r in artifacts if r.get('reason') == 'compiler-artifact']
arrow = [r for r in artifacts if r['target']['name'] == 'arrow_cast']
assert len(arrow) == 1
arrow = arrow[0]
assert Path(arrow['manifest_path']).parent == p.parent / 'integer-widening-sparse-owned-542a847/arrow-cast'
binaries = {}
for name, target in [('bench', 'decimal_bench'), ('probe', 'decimal_probe'), ('runner', 'delta-reader-sail-extraction-probe')]:
    matches = [r for r in artifacts if r['target']['name'] == target and r['executable']]
    assert len(matches) == 1

base = os.environ.copy()
assert not any(k.startswith(('MALLOC_', 'GLIBC_', 'LD_PRELOAD', 'DECIMAL_BENCH_')) for k in base)
order = ['before', 'after', 'reference', 'reference', 'after', 'before'] * 2
experiments = [(v, i, targets if v == 'reference' else controls + targets) for i, v in enumerate(order)]
runs = []
for variant, index, cases in experiments:
    for phase in (['planning', 'execution'] if index % 2 == 0 else ['execution', 'planning']):
        shift = index % len(cases)
        for case in cases[shift:] + cases[:shift]:
            directory = out / f'{index:02}-{variant}-{phase}-{case}'
            directory.mkdir()
            for name in ['control', 'ack']:
                os.mkfifo(directory / name)
            command = ['perf', 'stat', '--delay=-1', f'--control=fifo:{directory}/control,{directory}/ack', '--json-output', '-o', str(directory / 'counters.jsonl'), '-e', '{instructions:u,cycles:u},task-clock:u,context-switches:u,cpu-migrations:u,page-faults:u', '--', 'taskset', '-c', '2', str(p / f'{variant}-bench'), str(directory / 'capture.json'), 'subqueries', case]
            env = base | {'DECIMAL_BENCH_RETAIN': 'none', 'DECIMAL_BENCH_PERF_DIR': str(directory), 'DECIMAL_BENCH_PERF_PHASE': phase}
            result = subprocess.run(command, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, timeout=180)
            capture = json.loads((directory / 'capture.json').read_text())
            assert len(capture['results']) == 1
            r = capture['results'][0]
            for field, value in canonical[variant][case].items():
                assert r[field] == value, (variant, case, field)
            assert r['retention'] == 'none' and r['retained_rows'] == 0
            counters = [json.loads(x) for x in (directory / 'counters.jsonl').read_text().splitlines() if x.startswith('{')]
            assert len(counters) == 6 and all(x['pcnt-running'] == 100 for x in counters)
            assert result.stderr.count('Events enabled') == 1
            assert len(r['samples_ms']) == len(r['planning_samples_ms']) == 9
            samples = r['planning_samples_ms' if phase == 'planning' else 'samples_ms']
            runs.append({'variant': variant, 'phase': phase, 'index': index, 'case': case, 'command': command, 'capture': capture, 'counters': counters, 'median_ms': statistics.median(samples)})
    (p / 'performance.json').write_text(json.dumps({'order': order, 'controls': controls, 'targets': targets, 'runs': runs}, indent=2) + '\n')
    print(variant, index, 'complete', flush=True)


def stats(rows):
    medians = [r['median_ms'] for r in rows]
    instructions = [next(float(c['counter-value']) for c in r['counters'] if c['event'] == 'instructions:u') for r in rows]
    return {'processes': len(rows), 'median_ms': statistics.median(medians), 'process_medians_ms': medians, 'median_instructions': statistics.median(instructions), 'process_instructions': instructions}


summary = {}

    summary[phase] = {}
    for case in controls + targets:
        groups = {v: stats([r for r in runs if r['variant'] == v and r['case'] == case and r['phase'] == phase]) for v in ['before', 'after']}

        if case in targets:

import hashlib
import json
import os
import shutil
import time
from pathlib import Path

p = Path(__file__).parent
sha = lambda f: hashlib.sha256(Path(f).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
sources = json.loads((p / 'initial-sources.json').read_text())
executables = json.loads((p / 'initial-executables.json').read_text())
overrides = {'common.rs': p / 'candidate-common.rs'}
for key, record in sources.items():
    if key == 'physical-test-lock':
        assert not Path(record['path']).exists()
        continue
    expected = overrides.get(key, p / f'before-source-{key}')
    assert Path(record['path']).read_bytes() == expected.read_bytes(), key
    if record['existed']:
        assert sha(p / f'initial-{key}') == record['sha256'], key
for key, record in executables.items():
    expected = p / f'after-{key}'
    assert sha(record['path']) == sha(expected), key
    assert sha(p / f'initial-target-{key}') == record['sha256'], key

started = time.time()
restored = {'sources': {}, 'executables': {}}
for key, record in sources.items():
    file = Path(record['path'])
    if record['existed']:
        shutil.copyfile(p / f'initial-{key}', file)
        shutil.copymode(p / f'initial-{key}', file)
        os.utime(file, None)
        assert sha(file) == record['sha256']
        assert file.stat().st_mtime >= started
        restored['sources'][key] = {'sha256': sha(file), 'fresh_mtime': True}
    else:
        file.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        restored['sources'][key] = {'absent': True}
for key, record in executables.items():
    file = Path(record['path'])
    # Cargo sometimes links this path to an artifact in deps/. Unlink before
    # restoring so another artifact is never overwritten through the hardlink.
    file.unlink()
    shutil.copyfile(p / f'initial-target-{key}', file)
    file.chmod(0o755)
    assert sha(file) == record['sha256']
    restored['executables'][key] = {'sha256': sha(file), 'mode': '0755'}
(p / 'restoration.json').write_text(json.dumps(restored, indent=2) + '\n')
print('Restored all 37 sources/lockfiles and three executable slots.')
